answer: Reputation decays exponentially with a fixed temporal half-life, so identities must sustain honest service to retain trust. In the reciprocity-weighted EigenTrust graph, a freshly spawned sybil has almost no incoming trusted mass and thus near-zero eigenvector centrality; dividing activity among aliases cannot create credible paths. Temporal weighting prevents an inlet of mutual endorsements from flooding consensus through karst-like channels, and an umber badge or age claim alone grants no voting weight.
